facts_from_discussion: The parties stipulated that petitioner elected to take a full distribution from his retirement account in 2016.
The record includes District Court orders and other documents establishing that the distribution, after Federal and State income tax withholding, was credited to petitioner's restitution obligation.

The court found that the proceeds of the distribution were paid to petitioner and then, through Mr. Eisenhauer, transferred to his former employer (PCG) in partial satisfaction of his restitution obligation.
Petitioner does not dispute that his retirement plan trust was a qualified trust under section 401(a).
Petitioner neither argued nor established that any exception (e.g., rollover) to inclusion applies; he contends instead that he never received or benefited from the distribution.
Petitioner was not 59 1/2 years old at any time during 2016.

The court found that petitioner did not use the distribution for the payment of any expense (such as qualifying medical expenses) that would allow him to avoid the 10% additional tax; he did not argue that any other section 72(t) exception (such as disability) applies.
Petitioner argues he relied on Principal to withhold the correct amount of tax.
The parties agree that petitioner's 2016 return was not timely filed.
Petitioner was incarcerated from July 2016 until July 2017.

The court found credible petitioner's testimony that while incarcerated he attempted to comply with his filing obligation but was prevented from doing so; respondent offered no evidence to rebut that testimony.
Within days of his release in July 2017, petitioner sought the records he needed to prepare his return, which he filed in early September 2017.

The court found it more likely than not that petitioner would have filed a timely return or request for extension had he been able to do so, and found that petitioner was unable to file a return or a request for extension within the prescribed time despite exercising ordinary business care and prudence.
Respondent argued that petitioner, as a former C.P.A., knew the due date for his return.
